column1: # OmniWM settings: <table.key><TAB><TOML value>. Only keys that differ from
# Defaults already equal to niri: gaps 16, centerFocusedColumn "never",
# niri touchpad: 3 fingers sideways scroll columns, 3 fingers up/down switch
# workspaces, 4 fingers up opens the overview.
# Fingers move the content the other way round from OmniWM's default; this one
# switch flips both column scrolling and workspace swipes.
# The workspace bar (our Waybar) sits below the macOS menu bar instead of
# covering it, and tiled windows leave room for it.
# Workspace swipes draw their preview at the screensaver level; keep the bar
# at the same level so it stays visible instead of blinking on every swipe.
# niri keeps a lone window at its column width and never stretches columns to
# fill the screen; OmniWM's defaults ("fill", and widening columns while fewer
# than visibleContainerCount are open) do both. With a count of 1 the widening
# never applies; new columns still open at defaultContainerPrimarySpan (1/2).
# That key is optional and OmniWM can drop it when it saves; without it a new
# column takes 1/visibleContainerCount, the full screen, and Mod+F has nothing
# to toggle back to. So set it here rather than rely on the generated file.
# Place the bar ourselves: notch mode ignores the offsets. yOffset moves it
# down (negative) so the gap under the notch matches the gap to the windows.
# niri's `focus-follows-mouse`: focus follows the pointer without a click.
# kitty-new-window reads the layout through omniwmctl to open a window where
# OmniWM will put it (a local socket; only processes of this user can use it).
